t.E445.agn: In its 2018 re-evaluation EFSA temporarily maintained the acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 12.5 mg/kg body weight because no reproductive and developmental data were available, and limited the evaluation to the product made from Pinus palustris and Pinus elliottii pines. In its 2023 follow-up opinion, based on a new rat study, it set the ADI at 10 mg/kg body weight; it found no safety concern at the maximum permitted levels and at the reported uses, and recommended changes to the EU specifications (revision of the definition, lowering of the limits for toxic elements).
t.E445.body: Glycerol esters of wood rosin are largely not broken down in the gut; most are excreted unchanged in faeces. In rats at most 5% of the dose was absorbed; the absorbed part (most likely breakdown products of the monoesters) passes into the faeces via bile.
t.E445.found.2: Cloudy flavoured alcoholic drinks with less than 15% alcohol
t.E445.prod: It is produced by modifying a plant raw material through a chemical reaction.
t.E445.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI of 12.5 mg/kg temporarily maintained because reproductive/developmental data were lacking.
t.E445.regx.1: Follow-up opinion: ADI of 10 mg/kg body weight per day; applies only to the product from P. palustris and P. elliottii, no safety concern.
t.E445.summary: A weighting agent produced from pine resin. It helps disperse the flavouring in citrus-flavoured drinks.
t.E445.what: It is a stabiliser obtained from pine tree resin; in the EU it is authorised only in cloudy drinks.
